title: review: Fix-round delta: a Codex resume round also gets the Planner's fix spec
spec:
Goal T-1403, plan label D-fixdelta (human 2026-10-03 'do that'). Evidence 2026-10-03: fix rounds T-1631 and T-1633 (fix_round_for T-1629, Codex executor luna) were dispatched on the resume path; the executor saw only the parent's old gate log, never the Planner's fix spec, so T-1631 fixed the old log its own way (stubbed bus.read, rejected by review T-1632) and T-1633 changed nothing. gotchas.md 2026-10-03 'Codex resume fix rounds never see the fix task's spec'.

Facts (goal/T-1403; locate by symbol): the daemon dispatch loop, for a task with constraints.fix_round_for whose executor.resume_plan(parent, t) says mode 'resume', calls spawn_async(_dispatch_reply_worker, t['id'], parent['id'], _fix_round_delta(parent, t), plan). _fix_round_delta(parent, fix) returns 'Failures:\n' + parent resume_hint.failures (or the parent's rejecting review comments) capped at 3000 chars + '\n\nAcceptance:\n' + selected fix acceptance. It never reads fix['spec']. Auto rounds filed by auto_fix_round carry constraints.auto_round and a spec rendered from fix-round.md (which already contains the failure text); Planner-written fix rounds have no auto_round.

Change: in _fix_round_delta, when the fix task has no constraints.auto_round, prepend a section 'Fix-round instructions from the Planner (follow these; they supersede the failure text below):' followed by fix['spec'] capped at 6000 chars (append '\n[spec truncated]' when cut), then a blank line, then the existing Failures and Acceptance sections unchanged. Auto rounds (constraints.auto_round set) produce exactly the same delta as today. No other change.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): existing tests of _fix_round_delta (grep '_fix_round_delta' in tests/) pass unchanged for auto rounds; update any that build a Planner fix round without auto_round only if they pin the full delta text, and say so in the commit message. Commit first, then run tests/test_daemon.py in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_fix_round_delta_includes_planner_fix_spec: passes: for a fix task without constraints.auto_round whose spec is 'Remove the bus.read stubs', _fix_round_delta(parent, fix) starts with the Planner-instructions heading, contains that spec text before the 'Failures:' section, and still contains the parent's failures and the fix acceptance; a 7000-char spec is cut to 6000 chars plus '[spec truncated]'; for a fix task with constraints.auto_round 1 the delta equals the output of the unchanged code (no instructions heading, no spec text)

result.summary: The diff matches the spec. Planner fix rounds (no auto_round) get the heading and the spec before the unchanged Failures and Acceptance sections. The spec is cut at 6000 chars with '\n[spec truncated]' appended. Auto rounds return the old delta exactly. The new test covers the heading, spec before Failures, failures and acceptance still present, the truncation, and exact equality for the auto round. I only read the diff and did not run the tests.

comments.issue: The check is `"auto_round" not in constraints`, so a task with auto_round present but falsy (e.g. 0 or None) is treated as an auto round and gets no spec. The spec words it as 'has no constraints.auto_round', so this is a small difference. It matches how auto_fix_round files rounds, which start at 1.
